title: Certificates of Deposit: booking and pricing the renewal that falls due when grace ends
content:
## Situation this policy governs

On the day after the grace period ends, a Certificates of Deposit certificate that no grace action closed, and whose maturity instruction is automatic renewal, renews into its renewal tier. This policy prices such a renewal: the business result it governs is the interest rate of the new term. The renewal is booked with the tool described below, and the new term shows on the certificate record at once.

## Entry condition

The certificate carries an instruction to renew automatically at the moment its renewal is booked. A certificate renews only under an instruction to renew automatically, so a payout instruction that must be replaced is replaced before the renewal is booked; a certificate that does not carry such an instruction at that moment has no renewal written under this policy.

## Tool: renew_certificate_term_21cb639a

### What it does

The tool books a new term on a certificate of deposit that has reached maturity. The certificate becomes active again in the tier given, with the new term's start and maturity dates, the rate and APY fixed for the new term, and the two bonus markers for that term. The one bump-up allowed per term is made available again, and the certificate's renewal count goes up by one. The principal balance is not touched.

### How it is invoked

renew_certificate_term_21cb639a is an internal tool, unlocked first and then called by the agent.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format and allowed values |
|---|---|---|
| certificate_id | The certificate reference number being renewed, as returned by the certificate lookup for this customer | Identifier |
| variant_name | The tier of the new term | One of: 6-Month Certificate, 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate, 12-Month Certificate, 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate, 36-Month Certificate, 60-Month Certificate |
| term_start_date | First day of the new term | Calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD, never empty |
| maturity_date | The calendar date on which the new term matures | Calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD, never empty |
| interest_rate | The annual interest rate of the new term, bonuses included | Percent, 2 decimal places |
| apy | The annual percentage yield of the new term, bonuses included | Percent, 2 decimal places |
| jumbo_bonus_applied | Whether the jumbo bonus is part of the new term's rate | true (included) or false (not included) |
| relationship_bonus_applied | Whether the relationship bonus is part of the new term's rate | true (included) or false (not included) |

### What it returns

A successful call returns a receipt, rendered as text, with certificate_id (the certificate renewed), status (active), variant_name (tier of the new term), term_start_date and maturity_date (YYYY-MM-DD), interest_rate and apy (percent, 2 decimal places), jumbo_bonus_applied and relationship_bonus_applied (true or false), and renewal_count (the certificate's renewal count after this renewal, an integer). A receipt with status active means the new term is booked.

## Contract questions

**Does booking the renewal move money?**
No. The principal balance is not touched; the call changes the term, the rate, the APY and the markers.

**Does the tool work out the rate?**
No. It records the rate and APY supplied, each kept to 2 decimal places.
